facts.raw_span: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis
denied hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
complete right facial paralysis
nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
mild sensorineural loss at 4000 Hz
5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen
heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve
erosion of the posterior external auditory canal
expansion of the stylomastoid foramen
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67
Low cellularity and low MIB-1 proliferation index

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma, a type of benign tumor that arises from the Schwann cells of the facial nerve.
The patient's symptoms of gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis are consistent with facial paralysis, which can be caused by a variety of conditions, including Bell's palsy.
The patient's imaging findings of a mass in the mastoid area are consistent with a mastoid tumor, which can cause symptoms such as facial paralysis and hearing loss.

The patient's pathology findings of a tumor with pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and low cellularity are consistent with a schwannoma, a type of benign tumor that arises from the Schwann cells of the nerve.
It explains the expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve.
